option.1: A finished system with login, payments, and every user type
option.2: A twenty-page website with blog, shop, and an about section
option.3: A registered company that already serves paying customers
option.4: An early, incomplete version used to show the idea and learn
answerExplanation: A prototype is for showing and learning, not for running a full service. Login, many pages, and a live company are not what a first prototype is for.

contentBody: **How does a wireframe differ from a landing page?**
option.1: A wireframe is the box layout; a landing page is a real one-page link
option.2: A wireframe is the full product; a landing page is only a colour palette
option.3: A landing page must include login; a wireframe must include payments
option.4: They are the same artefact, so either word can replace the other
answerExplanation: A wireframe shows what sits where before decoration. A landing page is one screen with one story and one main action that someone can open.

contentBody: **What should the call-to-action on a first landing page be?**
option.1: Five equal buttons such as Login, Shop, Blog, About, and Contact
option.2: A Learn more label that does not open any real destination
option.3: One next step, as a button or link the visitor can actually use
option.4: A gallery of many images with no request for any action
answerExplanation: One primary CTA names the job (for example join a waitlist) and must work. Extra buttons split attention. A dead “learn more” is not a next step.

contentBody: **What does a website builder let you do?**
option.1: Write a full program before any words are chosen
option.2: Type the page into visual boxes and publish a link
option.3: Skip checking facts the model invented
option.4: Collect official identity numbers as the only form field
answerExplanation: Tools such as Google Sites, Canva, Carrd, or Durable let you assemble a page without writing a program. You still edit the words and you still avoid collecting private data you do not need.

contentBody: **Why keep an early waitlist form to a few fields such as name, context, and yes/no?**
option.1: A tiny form is enough to act; extra private fields are not needed yet
option.2: Official identity documents must be collected before any headline is written
option.3: A long survey is the only way a button can count as a call-to-action
option.4: Forms are optional if the page uses a dark theme and looks expensive
answerExplanation: The form is part of the prototype. A few honest fields let someone act. Passwords, identity numbers, and huge surveys do not belong on a first waitlist.
